subject: Waller floated a half-point hike after October's CPI
bodyMarkdown:
If you have a mortgage renewing in the next year, or you hold bonds in an RRSP, Tuesday's American inflation report made your money more expensive. The move in prices was small. The move in what traders expect from the Federal Reserve was not small at all.

## The number came in hot

The Bureau of Labor Statistics published October's Consumer Price Index on Tuesday morning. Prices rose 0.4 per cent from September, when economists had been looking for 0.3. **Core CPI**, which strips out food and energy to show the trend underneath, rose 0.3 per cent against a forecast of 0.2. That is the third month in a row core has printed 0.3. Run that pace for twelve months and you get about 3.7 per cent, nowhere near the Fed's 2 per cent target. September's headline had already come in at 0.6 per cent. Two hot months back to back stop being a blip, and I think that is what moved markets more than the October number on its own.

## The report with a hole in it

Here is the part I find strange. This release carried no annual inflation rate. The Bureau said it would not publish 12-month changes for October 2026 wherever October 2025 data do not exist, and for most of the basket they do not exist, because the shutdown that ran from October 1 to November 12 last year kept price collectors from going out. That month was never recovered. Gasoline still got a yearly figure, since its October 2025 value had been published. Everything else is a monthly change and nothing more. The last official annual readings are September's, at 3.7 per cent headline and 2.6 per cent core. So a shutdown that ended a year ago is still deleting numbers the Fed uses to set the rate on my parents' mortgage.

## Waller put fifty basis points on the table

Bloomberg reported on Tuesday that Fed governor Christopher Waller, who had been leaning toward a quarter-point increase in December, now says a half-point move should be considered. Dallas Fed president Lorie Logan said the committee needs at least two more quarter-point hikes. The target range sits at 3.75 to 4.00 per cent and the meeting is December 8 and 9. CNBC reported that CME's FedWatch odds of a half-point move climbed to roughly 14 per cent on the day, with a quarter point close to fully priced. Bonds did the rest. CNBC also reported the 10-year Treasury yield climbing back near 5 per cent after a weak auction. The S&P 500 closed down 0.38 per cent and the Nasdaq down 0.74 per cent, with Nvidia the biggest drag.

## The takeaway

The Bank of Canada decides on December 9, the same day the Fed finishes. It already raised to 2.5 per cent on October 28, and its deliberations, released Tuesday, said members agreed there could be a need to go further. Canadian five-year fixed mortgage rates follow the five-year Government of Canada bond, and that bond follows Washington more closely than most of us would like. If you are renewing before next summer, lock a rate hold this week instead of next month, and watch December 10, when the next American CPI lands.
